question: Which of the following cities is famous for the iconic 'Kumbh Mela'?
solution:
The correct answer is "Prayagraj". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• In Hinduism, Kumbh Mela is a major pilgrimage and festival. It is celebrated at four river-bank pilgrimage sites in a period of approximately 12 years: the Prayagraj (confluence of the Ganges-Yamuna Sarasvati rivers), Haridwar (Ganges), Nashik (Godavari), and Ujjain (Shipra).
 
• The festival is characterised by a ceremonial dip in the waters, but it is also a celebration of community exchange with various fairs, schooling, saintly religious discourses, monks or poor people's mass feedings, and entertainment displays.
 
• As part of his efforts to launch major Hindu gatherings for philosophical discussions and debates along with Hindu monasteries in the Indian subcontinent, the festival is historically attributed to the Hindu philosopher and Saint Adi Shankara of the 8th century.
 
• There is, however, no historical literary evidence before the 19th century of these mass pilgrimages called "Kumbha Mela".
 
• It has been inscribed on the UNESCO Official List of Humanity's Intangible Cultural Heritage.
